practices.practice: Create one long-lived MongoClient per process (singleton) and reuse it rather than opening a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single, long-lived MongoClient instance per process and reuse it for all requests (do not open a new client per request). Configure maxPoolSize to a reasonable value (e.g., 50) and set serverSelectionTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS to avoid blocking callers.

practices.practice: Keep the DocumentDB connection string and credentials out of source control; read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment (or an uncommitted config) and never log secrets.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the DocumentDB connection URI/credentials out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment variables (or from a config file that is not checked in). Never log the full URI or secrets.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Python

practices.practice: For production, store DB credentials or secrets in a managed secret store such as Azure Key Vault rather than embedding primary keys in code or sample fixtures.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer managed secret storage for production: store DB credentials in Azure Key Vault and fetch them at runtime, or use a deployment secret mechanism. Do not embed primary keys in code or sample fixtures.

practices.practice: Always use TLS for client connections and restrict network access with firewall rules or Private Endpoints/Private Link; prefer private connectivity for production clusters.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL on the client connection and enforce server certificate validation; restrict cluster access with firewall rules or VNet/IP allow lists so only app hosts can reach the cluster.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB security/connectivity FAQ; search: "Azure DocumentDB TLS Private Link firewall"

practices.practice: When building a RAG pipeline, store each chunk with document identifiers, chunk id, chunk text, embedding (if present), and metadata (title/source) so you can filter, attribute and retrieve without re-reading original documents.
practices.prior_belief: Design document schema for retrieval: store each chunk with fields {product_id, chunk_id, text, embedding: <float array>, length, source, metadata: {...}} so you can filter on metadata and compute scores without re-reading product docs.

practices.practice: When running a vector kNN ($search with cosmosSearch), push structured predicates into the search (filter/pre_filter) so filtering happens inside the ANN search rather than post-filtering client-side.
practices.prior_belief: Limit client-side scanning by applying server-side filters before computing embeddings/similarity (e.g., filter by product category or availability) to reduce vector-search cost and improve precision.

practices.practice: Store vectors as dense numeric arrays (number[]) so they are indexable by DocumentDB; include the embedding model name and the vector dimension as metadata so queries can validate compatibility.
practices.prior_belief: Use consistent serialization for vectors (store as dense arrays of numbers in a single field) and avoid storing vectors as nested documents or strings; index the array field as the vector index target.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector search docs; search: "vectors must be number[] Azure DocumentDB"

practices.practice: When creating vector indexes, pick the algorithm and parameters to match scale (vector-ivf for small demos, vector-hnsw for medium datasets, vector-diskann for large production), set the similarity metric that matches your query-time scoring, and tune index parameters (numLists / m / efConstruction / lSearch / maxDegree) to balance recall and latency.
practices.prior_belief: When enabling a vector index, specify the same distance metric used at query time (cosine/inner_product or euclidean) and configure index parameters appropriate for the size (e.g., HNSW efConstruction/efSearch values or IVF nlist). Ensure the vector index dimension matches stored vectors.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: search: "Azure DocumentDB vector index DiskANN HNSW IVF tuning"

practices.practice: Prefer DocumentDB's search index and $search aggregation (createSearchIndexes) for full-text features (BM25, fuzzy, phrase, custom analyzers) rather than relying on community MongoDB text indexes and $text.
practices.prior_belief: Create a scalar/index on commonly filtered fields such as product_id and any category/tags used for filtering, and create a text index for fallback keyword matching on chunk text (e.g., db.product_chunks.createIndex({text: 'text'})).
practices.how_found: search: "Azure DocumentDB full-text search createSearchIndexes vs text index"

practices.practice: Use explain()/query plan output and the DocumentDB tooling (Index Advisor / MCP list_indexes / explain) to verify index definitions, confirm index usage, and detect COLLSCANs or index-misses.
practices.prior_belief: If vector indexing or vector search configuration tools are needed, verify index creation with the cluster management tooling (MCP) and inspect query plans; have fallback text/search code path if vector index isn't present.
practices.source_name: Azure DocumentDB MCP Toolkit / How to read explain output

practices.practice: Implement retries for transient faults with exponential backoff and jitter, and make write operations idempotent (upserts or client-generated idempotency tokens) if they will be retried.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors (network timeouts, 5xx server errors). For writes that must be retried, ensure idempotency (use upserts or include a client-generated idempotency token field).
practices.how_found: search: "Azure DocumentDB transient faults retry exponential backoff"

practices.practice: Monitor index and query performance: enable diagnostic settings/slow-query logs, use explain() and Index Advisor recommendations, and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/connection saturation for your cluster tier.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor index usage and query performance (slow queries, index misses) and maintain an automated test that validates retrieval latency and recall for a small set of canonical queries after seeding.
practices.source_name: Manage indexing in Azure DocumentDB / Index Advisor
practices.how_found: search: "Index Advisor Azure DocumentDB explain query plan"

practices.practice: Use SDK bulk/ingestion features when ingesting large numbers of documents (AllowBulkExecution / bulk mode where available) or parallel async clients; be aware there are batch/write limits and tune concurrency to avoid throttling.
practices.source_name: Tips for optimizing vector indexing & search performance / bulk execution
practices.how_found: search: "Azure DocumentDB bulk ingestion AllowBulkExecution bulk mode"

practices.practice: Document size must not exceed 16 MB; design chunking and chunk-size to keep documents well under that limit.
practices.source_name: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: search: "Azure DocumentDB max document size 16 MB"

practices.practice: In RAG prompt engineering, retrieve a tuned top-N set of chunks, deduplicate/threshold them, and truncate or summarize the assembled context to fit the LLM token budget before calling the model.
practices.prior_belief: For RAG prompt engineering: retrieve top-N (e.g., 5) chunks, deduplicate and rank by combined vector score + metadata score, then truncate or select spans to ensure the assembled context fits the LLM token limit.
practices.how_found: search: "RAG prompt engineering manage context window Azure"

practices.practice: Record provenance metadata (source id, chunk index, source URL/timestamp) with each chunk so answers can cite sources and support traceability for RAG outputs.
practices.prior_belief: Store provenance metadata with each chunk (source doc id, chunk index, URL, timestamp) so generated answers can cite sources and allow traceability/auditing of RAG outputs.

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID and RBAC for authentication and least-privilege per-application users rather than long-lived primary/master keys; use key rotation and restrict permissions to required DB/collections.
practices.prior_belief: Rotate/roll keys periodically and avoid using primary/master key in long-lived deployments. If using read-only app credentials, restrict permissions to the required database/collections.
practices.how_found: search: "Azure DocumentDB Microsoft Entra ID RBAC least privilege"

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings for cosine similarity (e.g., L2-normalize) and record the embedding model and dimensions with each vector so query-time checks can avoid dimension mismatches.
Prefer creating indexes after large bulk ingestion to reduce write-time overhead; plan index lifecycle (hide -> drop) and keep a modest number of indexes per collection.
